headline_cluster.headline: התפתחות דרמטית: המצור האיראני נשבר, הישג עצום לארה"ב — נתונים חדשים מצביעים על זינוק נוסף ביצוא הנפט ושבירה בפועל של מנוף הלחץ האיראני העוצמתי ביותר

primary_source_candidates.source: Kpler provisional ship-tracking data on Middle East Gulf crude exports, as reported by Reuters (Oct 4-5, 2026)
primary_source_candidates.access: Kpler terminal data is subscription-only; Reuters wire carried the figures. WebFetch to aljazeera.com, newarab.com, cnbc.com, gcaptain.com and businesstoday.in all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED; figures taken from consistent WebSearch snippets of multiple Reuters re-publications.

primary_source_candidates.source: Kpler blog: 'EXPLAINER: How Mideast Gulf crude exports returned to pre-war levels'
primary_source_candidates.access: WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED; content read via WebSearch snippet only

verified_figures_summary: Kpler (provisional): Middle East crude exports reached 19.5-22.5 mb/d on Sep 24 and Sep 27-29; 7-day moving average 18.5 mb/d on Oct 1 vs ~18 mb/d pre-war average (Mar 2025-Feb 2026), i.e. ~+0.5 mb/d (~3%). Sept: at least 16.5 mb/d left the region, matching the pre-war average excluding Iran. Iran itself is the exception: no new crude loaded at Iranian terminals since mid-Aug (US counter-blockade), production ~1.8 mb/d, about half pre-war. Routes changed: 40% of Gulf crude now bypasses Hormuz (17% pre-war); of what crosses, >70% is ship-to-ship transferred off Fujairah/Sohar; Iraqi tankers transit with Iranian permission; tanker attacks increasing; refined-fuel shipments still constrained.
scope_correction: Search snippet of the article's own title ('המצור האיראני נשבר: יצוא הנפט מהמפרץ הפרסי גבוה משהיה לפני המלחמה') shows the claim is about PERSIAN GULF (overwhelmingly non-Iranian) crude exports exceeding pre-war levels despite Iran's Hormuz blockade — not about Iran's own oil exports. 'Iranian blockade' = Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The task brief's gist ('Iran's oil exports') was a misreading; Iran's own exports actually collapsed.
detect_exclusion_check: Not excluded: claim concerns crude export VOLUME (commodity flow data), not oil prices/market data.
clustering_note: single-outlet item; no corroborating cluster found across the other 7 reachable outlets in this run

claims.location: headline (figures per search snippet of article)
claims.claim: New data show Persian Gulf crude exports now exceed pre-war levels: 7-day moving average 18.5 mb/d on Oct 1 vs 18 mb/d before the war
claims.verified_figure: Kpler (provisional, via Reuters): 7-day MA 18.5 mb/d on Oct 1 vs ~18 mb/d pre-war average (Mar 2025-Feb 2026)
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 18.5 mb/d 7-day average on Oct 1 vs 18 mb/d pre-war; some days up to 22.5 mb/d; attributed to Kpler data published by Reuters
claims.note: Figures match the Kpler/Reuters numbers exactly. Checked only via search snippet since the article body is blocked; 'provisional' caveat not verifiable in the body.

claims.claim: 'נתונים חדשים מצביעים על זינוק נוסף ביצוא הנפט' — new data point to a further jump in oil exports
claims.verified_figure: 7-day MA ~+0.5 mb/d (~3%) above pre-war; 19.5-22.5 mb/d only on four individual days (Sep 24, 27-29); provisional data; the rise is Gulf exports ex-Iran, while Iran's own exports have fallen to near zero
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 18.5 vs 18 mb/d; up to 22.5 mb/d on some days
claims.note: Directionally correct (Gulf exports recovered and rose), but the homepage headline omits whose exports (Gulf producers, not Iran — in context with 'Iranian blockade' readers can easily read it as Iranian exports, which actually collapsed), the pre-war baseline, and that the 'jump' is ~3% on the 7-day average with the larger figures being single-day provisional peaks.

claims.claim: The data show the Iranian blockade 'is broken' — 'שבירה בפועל של מנוף הלחץ האיראני העוצמתי ביותר' (effective breaking of Iran's most powerful leverage)
claims.verified_figure: Kpler: crude volumes back at/slightly above pre-war, but 40% of Gulf crude now bypasses Hormuz (vs 17%); most crude crossing is shuttled via ship-to-ship transfers; Iraqi flows pass with Iranian permission; tanker attacks increasing; refined-product exports still constrained; reports of Iran charging transit tolls
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 18.5 vs 18 mb/d presented as evidence of American success in breaking the Iranian blockade
claims.note: Conclusion inferred from data, so in scope. The source shows volume recovery achieved largely by routing around Hormuz and via escorted/shuttle workarounds, with Iran still controlling Iraqi passage and attacks rising — not that Iran's leverage over the strait has been 'effectively broken'. Editorial framing ('התפתחות דרמטית', 'הישג עצום לארה"ב') not judged.
